newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Defiance shares valued at A$2.65-A$2.85.
newsitem.headline: Defiance shares valued at A$2.65-A$2.85.

text.p: Baking and milling group Defiance Mills Ltd said on Tuesday an independent report prepared by Price Waterhouse for its Part B reply to Bunge Corp's A$1.70 a share takeover offer had valued Defiance's shares at between A$2.65 to A$2.85.

Defiance's directors repeated their view that shareholders should reject the Bunge bid because it was too low and said Price Waterhouse had also concluded that the bid was neither fair nor reasonable.

"Price Waterhouse has valued Defiance ordinary shares at between A$2.65 and A$2.85 per share, with a midpoint value of A$2.75 per share, including a control premium," Defiance said in its Part B response.
Price Waterhouse had said that the Bunge bid appeared not include a takeover premium, Defiance said. Defiance's shares were up five cents at A$1.95 at 11.25 a.m. (0125 GMT).

"Bunge's takeover offer makes no allowance for the conditional sale of the Defiance New Zealand assets and the value this transaction adds to, and implies for, Defiance's total assets," Defiance said.
Defiance agreed to sell its New Zealand milling and baking operations to fellow food group Goodman Fielder Ltd last month for NZ$48 million.
"Bunge's takeover offer does not reflect the value of Defiance's major brands and the goodwill, competitive position and market strength of those bra
Bunge is bidding A$2.10 cash for Defiance's Australian preference shares and NZ$2.07 cash for Defiance's New Zealand preference shares.
Bunge said when it made its takeover bid on March 4 that its A$97 million bid represented a mutliple of 20.6 times net income in calendar 1996 and 12.3 times pre-tax and interest earnings.

Bunge Foods Queensland Pty Ltd, which is the Bunge unit making the offer, is being advised by Merrill Lynch and has been in Australia since 1923. It now has two operating divisions involved in cereal foods and meat.
The Bunge parent company is based in Sao Paolo, Brazil and says it is the leading wheat miller in South America and a major global oilseed producer.
In a later statement, Defiance said it expected profit after tax and abnormals would rise 85 percent to A$6.3 million in the year to June 30, 1997.

"Even without the control premium for a full takeover offer the Price Waterhouse Corporate report values ordinary shares at between A$2.07 and A$2.15, again significantly in excess of the Bunge offer of A$1.70," Defiance Chairman Tom O'Brien said in the statement. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
